questions.question_text:
A site plan is drawn to a scale of $1:300$.
A rectangular block on the plan measures $8$ cm by $5$ cm.
Find the real area of the block, in square metres.

options.why: Scaled the plan area by the linear factor, $40\times300=12\,000\text{ cm}^{2}$, instead of by $300^{2}$.
Scaled the area by $300^{2}$ correctly but left the answer in square centimetres instead of converting to square metres.
Found the real perimeter, $2(24+15)$, instead of the real area.

questions.question_text:
A plan of a rectangular warehouse is drawn to a scale of $1:150$.
On the plan the warehouse measures $7$ cm by $4$ cm.
Find the real floor area, in square metres.

options.why: Multiplied the plan lengths, giving $28\text{ cm}^{2}$, and labelled this as square metres without applying the scale.
Multiplied the scaled lengths in centimetres, giving $630\,000\text{ cm}^{2}$, and labelled the result as square metres without converting.
Found the real perimeter, $2(10.5+6)$, instead of the real floor area.

questions.question_text:
A rectangular swimming pool is $54$ m long in real life.
On a scale diagram it measures $3.6$ cm long and $1.7$ cm wide.
Find the real area of the pool, to the nearest square metre.

options.why: Found the real perimeter, $2(54+25.5)$, instead of the real area.
Used the known length for both dimensions, calculating $54\times54$.
Multiplied the real lengths in centimetres, $5400\times2550$, and labelled the square-centimetre result as square metres without converting.

questions.solution_text:
$54\text{ m}=5400\text{ cm}$
$\text{scale factor}=3.6:5400=1:1500$
$\text{width}=1.7\times1500=2550\text{ cm}=25.5\text{ m}$
$A=54\times25.5$
$=1377\text{ m}^{2}$

questions.question_text:
A floor plan is drawn to a scale of $1:80$.
The rectangular shaded part of a kitchen measures $4.5$ cm by $3$ cm on the plan.
Find its actual perimeter, in metres.

options.why: Added the real length and width once, $3.6+2.4$, forgetting that the rectangle has two of each.
Found the perimeter in centimetres and labelled it as metres without dividing by $100$.
Multiplied the real length and width, giving an area of $8.64\text{ m}^{2}$, and labelled it as a perimeter in metres.

questions.question_text:
On a floor plan, a scale bar of length $2$ cm represents $1.5$ m.
The rectangular shaded part of a kitchen measures $8.4$ cm by $5.6$ cm on the plan.
Find its actual perimeter, in metres.

options.why: Multiplied the real length and width, $6.3\times4.2=26.46\text{ m}^{2}$, and labelled the area as a perimeter in metres.
Added the real length and width once, $6.3+4.2=10.5\text{ m}$, forgetting that a rectangle has two of each.
Found the perimeter in centimetres, $2(630+420)=2100\text{ cm}$, and labelled it as metres without dividing by $100$.

questions.solution_text:
$1\text{ cm represents }1.5\div2=0.75\text{ m}$
$\text{length}=8.4\times0.75=6.3\text{ m}$
$\text{width}=5.6\times0.75=4.2\text{ m}$
$P=2(6.3+4.2)$
$=2\times10.5$
$=21\text{ m}$

questions.question_text:
A floor plan gives all measurements in millimetres.
A rectangular garage measures $6000$ mm by $3600$ mm.
Find the floor area of the garage, in square metres.

options.why: Multiplied the two millimetre lengths and did not convert square millimetres to square metres.
Converted square millimetres to square metres by dividing by $1000$ instead of by $1\,000\,000$.
Found the perimeter of the garage instead of its area.

questions.question_text:
A map is drawn to a scale of $1:4000$.
A rectangular cemetery measures $3$ cm by $1.5$ cm on the map.
Find its real area, in square metres.

options.why: Multiplied the map lengths, giving $4.5\text{ cm}^{2}$, and labelled this as square metres without applying the scale.
Multiplied the map area by the linear factor $4000$ instead of scaling both lengths, then converted $18\,000\text{ cm}^{2}$ to square metres.
Found the real perimeter, $2(120+60)$, and labelled it as an area in square metres.

questions.question_text:
On an aerial photograph, a scale bar of length $1.2$ cm represents $45$ m.
A rectangular field measures $4.6$ cm by $2.8$ cm on the photograph.
Find its real area, to the nearest square metre.

options.why: Rounded the scale-bar length from $1.2$ cm to $1$ cm before calculating, so used $45$ m per centimetre and obtained $207\times126=26\,082\text{ m}^{2}$.
Found the real perimeter, $2(172.5+105)$, and labelled it as an area in square metres.
Rounded the real length from $172.5$ m to $173$ m before multiplying by the width of $105$ m.

questions.solution_text:
$1\text{ cm represents }45\div1.2=37.5\text{ m}$
$\text{length}=4.6\times37.5=172.5\text{ m}$
$\text{width}=2.8\times37.5=105\text{ m}$
$A=172.5\times105$
$=18\,112.5\text{ m}^{2}$
$\approx18\,113\text{ m}^{2}$
